clue.text: Serve a quick pint, but cheat

definitions.meaning: a barman draws (pulls) a pint speedily: pulls a fast one, the one being a pint

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: pulling a pint is drawing beer from the pump, so a quick one is a 'fast one'. The second is the idiom for tricking someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to deceive someone with a sly trick, which is what a cheat does.

clue.text: Cheers increase in fringe benefits

definitions.meaning: read literally, more perks on top

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: perks are fringe benefits, and 'up' says they rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To brighten in mood is to cheer up; read as two words it is extra job benefits going up.

clue.text: Pull fish up into the shelter of the boat

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to draw is to pull
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Hauling a catch aboard into the lee of the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole of DRAWEEL backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The leeward side of a vessel is the side away from the wind, so it is sheltered.

clue.text: Agreed people need time to make amends

parts.note: at one means in agreement
men are people

explanation.surface: Folk who have reached a settlement need a while to make up for wrongs.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonement is reparation for a wrong, the making of amends.

clue.text: Misbehave as a result of current setback

parts.note: AC is alternating current

indicators.note: joined to set, it tells us that word is read backwards

parts.note: to put is to set down

explanation.surface: Acting badly because of a recent setback.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'back' is the tail of the one printed word 'setback', whose first half is the piece it turns.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to behave badly, as a child or machine does.

clue.text: I take Patricia back edible tuber to make dessert

indicators.note: the short name is turned around

parts.note: Pat is short for Patricia
oca is a South American plant grown for its edible tuber

explanation.surface: Someone takes Patricia home and cooks a root vegetable pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PAT into TAP. Oca is an Andean root crop, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapioca, starch pearls from cassava, is cooked with milk as a pudding, a dessert.

clue.text: Auditor in the snuggery is as close as one can get

definitions.text: as close as one can get

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a nest is a snug, cosy place
an auditor is a listener, so the hearing organ, the ear

explanation.surface: An accountant cosily settled in the pub's snug, very close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant, and 'snuggery' like the cosy pub room; here one is literally a hearer and the other a cosy home. 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearest is the superlative of near, so the closest possible.

clue.text: Talk and make criticisms-nonsense!

parts.note: to utter is to speak
to rubbish something is to criticise it harshly

explanation.surface: Someone speaks and finds fault, then dismisses it all as rot.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter rubbish is complete nonsense, a dismissive exclamation.

clue.text: Missile blows poor Ted to pieces

indicators.note: blown to pieces, the letters of the two words are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A missile blasts some unfortunate fellow called Ted apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pieces' rearranges POORTED, the letters of 'poor Ted'.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled underwater weapon fired from a submarine or ship is a kind of missile.

clue.text: The highest price to get gas

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly, to prate

explanation.surface: Paying the most to fill up with petrol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gas' looks like fuel in an American sense, but here it is the verb meaning to talk at length.
explanation.definitionFit: The top rate of a charge or tax is its highest level, the maximum price.

clue.text: I present ring designed when full of initiative

indicators.note: the letters are designed into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone offers a ring of their own design, showing real initiative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges the twelve letters of 'I present ring'.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprising person shows initiative and resourcefulness.

clue.text: Subjugate East Balkans inhabitant in the North-East

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, as the inhabitant is placed in the region

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east
a Slav, such as a Serb or Croat, lives in the Balkans

explanation.surface: A geopolitical note about conquering a people living in the north-eastern Balkans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; compass points give the two single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To subjugate a people is to bring them under control, effectively to make them slaves.

clue.text: Be proud to produce a plan

definitions.meaning: proud here means sticking out from a surface, so to be proud is to jut out

explanation.walkthrough: 'proud' is used in the builder's sense of standing out from a surface, not of feeling pride.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to protrude or stick out; the noun is a planned undertaking or scheme.

clue.text: Penny goes into the attack fast

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, as an attacker goes in

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack

explanation.surface: A military report: a small coin's worth of force joins a swift assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes into' puts P inside RAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid and fast are synonyms meaning quick-moving.

clue.text: Always the first woman to beam

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible
a rafter is a roof beam

explanation.surface: Eve, the original woman, forever smiling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beam' tempts as a smile; it is the timber.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase, as in 'happily ever after', means for all time, which is always.

clue.text: Explained how former partner got punched up

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
pounded means hit repeatedly, punched

explanation.surface: An account of how an ex-spouse got beaten up.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound a theory is to set it out in detail, so explained.

clue.text: Mentioned that friar should get elevated

explanation.walkthrough: The words 'that friar should get' are surface padding: a friar is called Brother, and the phrase plays on a brother being raised up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both raised as a subject in talk and lifted to a higher position.

clue.text: Old Arab sultanate admits abstemious Turk

indicators.note: the outer letters let the other piece in

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula
TT means teetotal, abstaining from drink

explanation.surface: A historical note: an Arab state takes in a sober Turk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' is the container signal; teetotal is abbreviated TT in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottoman describes a Turk of the empire founded by Osman I.

clue.text: Sugar companies invested in any sticky stuff

indicators.note: a financial phrase here meaning placed within

parts.note: glue is any adhesive
COS is the plural abbreviation of company

explanation.surface: Firms putting money into adhesives, a sweet deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' reads as finance but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Glucose is a simple sugar found in blood and fruit.

clue.text: The last month to acquire alternative furnishings

parts.note: Dec is short for December, the last month of the year
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Buying new furniture for the home at year's end.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the style of furnishing and decoration of a room.

clue.text: Somehow I plod to get degree or college award

indicators.note: the letters are put together in some new way

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A student plods on to earn a qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges I PLOD into DIPLO.
explanation.definitionFit: A diploma is a certificate awarded by a college for completing a course.

clue.text: Brusque affirmation arising from gesture of respect

parts.note: curt means abrupt, brusque

indicators.note: in a down clue, the word rises, reading from the bottom

parts.note: yes is an affirmation

explanation.surface: A gruff yes rising out of a polite bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' turns YES to SEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtsey is a bob made by bending the knees as a sign of respect.

clue.text: Not out to get a loan, but still corresponding

parts.note: in cricket a batsman not out is in
to touch someone is slang for asking them to lend money

explanation.surface: A batsman still at the crease borrowing cash while keeping up letters.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'touch' someone for money is old British slang for borrowing from them.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay in touch with someone is to keep up contact by letter or call, still writing to them.

clue.text: Hesitation about sanction is balderdash

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: hum, as in hum and haw, is hesitation
to OK something is to approve it

explanation.surface: Dithering over approval is just nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'hum and haw' is the British phrase for dithering.
explanation.definitionFit: Hokum is nonsense, bunkum, balderdash.

clue.text: Judges a politician with rage in America

indicators.note: these pieces are put inside the country's abbreviation

parts.note: US is short for the United States
an MP is a Member of Parliament
ire is anger, rage

explanation.surface: Judges an angry politician over in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal, with the two inner pieces kept in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpires are officials who judge disputes or games, so the plural matches the verb-like plural noun.

clue.text: Pledge about a couple of thousand for main accommodation

indicators.note: the pledge word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to hock something is to pawn it, pledging it for a loan
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two are MM

explanation.surface: Pawning something for a couple of grand to pay for one's lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. 'main' is the sea, so this is a sailor's bed aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanging canvas bed was the traditional sleeping place of sailors at sea, the main.

clue.text: Calls to abandon ungodly behaviour

parts.note: to drop something is to abandon it
sin is wrongdoing against God

explanation.surface: A preacher's call to turn away from wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calls' looks like a summons; it means visits casually.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop in on someone is to pay them a casual visit, to call.

clue.text: Agent arranged itinerary around the Mediterranean

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the sea's short name
the letters of the word are put in a new order, as an itinerary is planned

parts.note: the Med is the usual short name for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A travel agent organises a trip round the Med.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' gives INTERIARY from the letters of the travel plan, and 'around' wraps them round the sea's short name.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent acting between two parties is a go-between or middleman.
